sources.fullCitation: Henner Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik 1925–1945. 10 vols. Uelzen: self-published; from vol. 2 Leverkusen: Pfau, 1987–2018. Vol. 6, (Foxtrott u.ä.) L–Q (2003), p. 780, entry “Mit dir möchte ich ziehn bis zum Ende der Welt”, marked SF for slow fox: Germany, 1931, music Kaper, Dr. B., words Rotter, Fritz, with the remark “Details unbekannt”. One disc is listed: EDBEL, catalogue number F 681, Orchester Dittke, the plus sign after the band name marking a vocal refrain. Digitised in the Digitale Bibliothek Thüringen from the copy in the Lippmann + Rau-Musikarchiv.
sources.title: Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik 1925–1945, vol. 6: (Foxtrott u.ä.) L–Q
sources.creator: Henner Pfau
sources.researchNote: The citation as first recorded named eight volumes dated 1987 and carried the DOI of vol. 1, which covers titles A–C; the set runs to ten volumes published between 1987 and 2018, and the entry stands in vol. 6 of 2003. The lexicon's own guide explains its conventions: SF marks a slow fox, and a plus sign after an orchestra name means the side carries a vocal. Its label key covers only the principal labels and does not expand EDBEL, so the issuing label behind that abbreviation is not settled here. The title is absent from the German national bibliography, the discographic title lists and the indexes of printed song collections, and no transfer of the disc has been traced; a similar but distinct title, “Mit dir möcht' ich geh'n bis an's Ende der Welt”, was composed by J. Pfeil and recorded in 1938.
